newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.150 cent per lb higher to 0.150 lower while pork bellies were called steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Steady to mostly higher cash hog indications linked to light hog runs and increased packer demand should boost hog futures somewhat, some sources said. They noted that cash loin prices have improved and supported pork cutout values which in turn, brightened packers' operating outlook, analysts said.
USDA reported cutout values $0.32 to $0.30 per cwt higher Monday.
However, expectations of weaker cash still prevail.
Some analysts expect increased hog runs when farmers finish spring planting which could weigh on futures at times.
A weak tone to cash bellies was expected to weigh on pork belly futures. Relatively high prices again shut off domestic demand, they said.
USDA reported 14-16 lb cash bellies $1 per cwt lower at $80 to $81 in the closing wire.

Uncertainty over Tuesday afternoon's out-of-town report may also weigh on futures. Traders and analysts cited talk of product moving into storage last week, but were uncertain over any out-movement, they said.
Having product go into storage despite the recent light slaughter would be bearish, they added.
Estimates on the report ranged from a net in of 1.0 million lbs to out 300,000 lbs.
